sections.title: Rainbow
sections.text: Rainbows form when sunlight interacts with water droplets in the atmosphere. As light enters a droplet, it refracts—bending the light—and reflects off the back of the droplet. This process separates the light into its component colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The reflected light exits the droplet at a slightly different angle, creating a circular arc of color in the sky. The exact shape and color intensity depend on the size and distribution of the droplets and the angle of the sunlight.
